Let <MATH_0001> be a locally Noetherian scheme. Let
<MATH_0002>
be a functor. Assume that
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0003> is representable
(as a transformation of functors, see
Categories, Definition <REF_0001>),
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0004> satisfies axioms [-1], [0], [1], [2], [3], [4], [5]
(see above), and
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0005> is a G-ring for all finite type points <MATH_0006> of <MATH_0007>.
<STRUCT_0005>
Then there exists a unique algebraic space
<MATH_0008>
whose restriction to <MATH_0009> is <MATH_0010>
(see proof for elucidation).

Recall that the sites <MATH_0001> and <MATH_0002> have the same
underlying category, see discussion in Section <REF_0001>.
Similarly the sites <MATH_0003> and
<MATH_0004> have the same underlying categories.
By axioms [0] and [1] the functor <MATH_0005> is a sheaf and
limit preserving.
Let <MATH_0006>
be the unique extension of <MATH_0007> which is a sheaf (for the <ACCENT_0001>tale topology)
and which is limit preserving, see
Lemma <REF_0002>.
Then <MATH_0008> satisfies axioms [0] and [1] as given in
Section <REF_0003>.
By Lemma <REF_0004> we see that
<MATH_0009> is representable (by schemes).
On the other hand, it is immediately clear that
<MATH_0010> satisfies axioms [-1], [2], [3], [4], [5] of
Section <REF_0005>
as each of these involves only evaluating <MATH_0011> at objects
of <MATH_0012> and we've assumed the
corresponding conditions for <MATH_0013>.
Whence <MATH_0014> is an algebraic space by
Proposition <REF_0006>.
